trial_court: Court of Civil Judge-06, (Central), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi - CS SCJ No. : 2271/18

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: ICICI Bank Limited, Through its Authorized Representative Sh. Mohit Grover
parties.respondent_defendant: Nar Singh, S/o Sh. Lal Bachan

facts_of_case: ICICI Bank Ltd filed a suit for recovery of Rs. 59,533/- along with interest @ 23.28% P.A. against Nar Singh, who had defaulted in repayment of loan amount and failed to pay EMI's.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the defendant to prove that the notice was not received.
legal_principles.held: When after several requests and reminders to the defendant for payment of loan amount, the plaintiff bank was compelled to serve notice dated 15.03.2018 to the defendant recalling/foreclosing the entire loan agreement but despite receipt of the notice, the defendant neither cared to reply to the said notice nor made any effort to repay the outstanding amount.

legal_principles.principle: The authenticity and correctness of the account statement can be established through a certificate under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act.
legal_principles.held: The Account Statement Ex.PW1/7, which is duly accompanied with certificate under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, establishes the factum of grant of loan to the defendant.

outcome.final_order: The final court order directed the defendant to repay the loan amount with interest.

use_for_drafting: drafting a suit for debt recovery
